criteria.given: Workflow references identify versioned artifact items, while explicit Git/hash inspection may expose raw source identities
then: Ordinary workflow references use qualified numeric item IDs and numeric revisions with explicit or inherited owner/type/parent context; hash prefixes are not the default domain identifiers
Any abbreviated raw Git/hash inspection declares its scope, expands colliding displays, and rejects ambiguous input without rebinding
Exact Git operations receive full object IDs resolved from separate integrity data; neither numeric references nor hash prefixes supply integrity authority
criteria.when: The system creates, persists, renders, and resolves default workflow references or explicitly requested Git/hash identities

criteria.given: Specs and their parts/requirements, plans and their items, tasks, and tests have numeric local IDs, related parent contexts, revisions, and legacy identifiers
then: New artifact/item IDs are unpadded positive local numbers qualified by work, type, and their declared related parent identities; numeric components sort numerically
Each artifact/item version has a positive numeric revision distinct from its stable logical identity; published identities and revision targets are immutable and never recycled or rebound
Local shorthand inherits only explicitly declared context; cross-workstream references name the owner and insufficient owner/type/parent/revision context fails
Parent prefixes express ownership rather than all dependency edges; multiple upstream dependencies remain explicit without duplicating logical items
Ancestor revision or unrelated repository changes alone do not rename or revise descendants; meaningful item content or binding changes publish a fresh item revision
Legacy mappings remain stable; moves require explicit historical mappings rather than guessing or retargeting old references
criteria.when: Items and versions are created, displayed, persisted, moved, and resolved across workstreams

criteria.given: Workflow records reference numeric artifact/item revisions and repeat contract, policy, source, review, or output integrity data under known semantics
then: A separate integrity file maps each qualified numeric item/revision reference to immutable full integrity data; ordinary spec/plan/task/test/report records use numeric references rather than embedded hashes

Committed item revisions resolve exact Git snapshots, repository-relative paths, and stable item IDs; shared source identities are stored once and Git content identity may avoid redundant generated item checksums
Required exact-byte and canonical-JSON checks retain full authoritative digests with explicit algorithm and semantics in the separate file

Evidence outside Git retains retrievable artifacts and full authoritative digests registered once per workstream, algorithm, and semantics where safely reusable; edited output invalidates its evidence
Missing or changed integrity entries cannot verify or rebind a published revision; numeric references alone confer no verification or acceptance authority
criteria.when: New-format records and their separate integrity file are registered and downstream reports are generated

criteria.given: A coordinator has accepted exact contract obligations and a candidate can edit its own JSON files and aliases
then: Resolution remains anchored to coordinator-owned accepted-tests authority and registered review/run records
Candidate-only modifications cannot authorize changed obligations or independent decisions
The existing exact intent approval and attributable independent review requirements remain enforced
criteria.when: The candidate replaces a manifest, changes a referenced contract, or claims independent approval

criteria.given: An accepted contract revision has historical evidence and a later run produces new logs
then: Adding run evidence leaves published contract entries unchanged
Contract pins and run/evidence records have separate immutable lifetimes
Historical references retain their original meaning; evidence for stale obligations cannot satisfy a different accepted contract
criteria.when: New contract and evidence records are registered and old references are reloaded

criteria.given: Committed structured items have deterministic comparison rules and byte-bound intent/log evidence retains exact-byte semantics
then: Structured content comparisons preserve declared canonical JSON equivalence, while artifact-item impact follows SH-07 and SH-16
Intent approval and byte-bound log verification preserve exact-byte invalidation
Where checksums are retained, algorithm and digest semantics remain explicit; display prefixes and different semantics cannot be substituted
criteria.when: JSON whitespace or key order changes, or exact artifact bytes change

criteria.given: A qualified numeric artifact/item revision resolves through the separate integrity file to a pinned Git snapshot, repository-relative path, and stable artifact item ID
then: Identical Git blob IDs provide an unchanged-content fast path; differing blobs trigger deterministic referenced-item content and binding comparison
Repository commit, file last-modifying commit, and ancestor revision changes alone do not establish item staleness or require a fresh item revision
Unrelated section edits and permitted formatting/reordering do not invalidate unchanged items; exact-byte approval/evidence rules remain enforced
Moves require explicit path resolution and stable IDs; ambiguous IDs, unsafe paths, missing objects, and unavailable documents fail without fallback to HEAD or worktree bytes
An absent item in an available candidate document enters deletion assessment; unavailable documents or objects are not inferred deletions
criteria.when: Recorded and candidate snapshots have identical blobs, unrelated section changes, relevant item changes, moved items, or unavailable targets

criteria.given: Workstreams, parents, and branches have overlapping local item/revision numbers, stale concurrent registrations, malformed references, and cyclic targets
then: References resolve by sufficient work, record type, related parent chain, stable item, and exact numeric revision context
Registration serializes ID/revision allocation and rejects stale conflicting publication or allocates a fresh unpublished identity/revision; existing revision entries remain immutable
Existing identities remain unchanged and missing, ambiguous, cyclic, or malformed references fail with a stable scoped reason
criteria.when: The coordinator registers or resolves records

criteria.given: Equivalent workflow data includes absent, null, empty, Unicode, and repeated shared-context values
then: Generated workflow JSON uses compact versioned serialization with shared context recorded once per group
Values and required evidence survive normalization; only schema-declared defaults permit field omission
Canonical validation is deterministic and absent, null, and empty remain distinguishable where required
criteria.when: New writers serialize it and supported readers normalize and validate it

criteria.given: Legacy and new records contain actual approvals, executions, Git dependencies, and provenance
then: Supported legacy records remain readable without rewriting history
Migration preserves originals and provenance, maps legacy IDs to numeric item/revision references only with exact source bindings, and never invents approval, execution, or Red/Green history
Export includes required immutable records and Git objects, or reports missing dependencies and refuses verified completeness
Unsupported versions and incomplete imports fail with explicit migration or availability reasons
criteria.when: Records are read, explicitly migrated, exported, and reloaded

criteria.given: An agent needs a spec/part, plan/item, task/test, status, or selected review/execution evidence from a large workstream
then: The projection supplies qualified numeric item/revision references and sufficient declared context; requested source/integrity evidence is resolved from the separate file on demand
The complete integrity catalog is not loaded by default
Failure output identifies unresolved references and scope; detailed evidence remains retrievable
criteria.when: The agent requests a compact projection and follows references needed for its task

criteria.given: Before implementation a corpus, source baseline, tokenizer identity/version, and deterministic equivalent workloads are frozen as specified in the Markdown proposal
then: Token totals include all necessary agent inputs and reference lookup responses; metadata byte totals include shared catalogs
All required evidence and equivalent questions are retained, using representative real workflow artifacts as well as collision fixtures
Aggregate input tokens and generated metadata JSON bytes are both strictly lower than baseline
The report records exact baseline/candidate identities, workload and tokenizer versions, per-journey totals, aggregate totals, individual regressions, and retained full-value exceptions
criteria.when: Baseline and new resume, independent-review, and completion journeys are measured with the same tokenizer

criteria.given: A record publication or coordinator registration is interrupted and then retried
then: Readers observe complete old or complete new published state and never a successful dangling reference
Retries preserve existing immutable targets and reject conflicting stale state
Fixture locks, processes, runtime files, and worktrees are cleaned without leaving real source changes uncommitted
criteria.when: Readers load the registry and the coordinator recovers the operation

criteria.given: An isolated end-to-end workflow accepts contracts, executes tests, registers independent review, and retains source/log/runner identities
then: Valid evidence retains the existing completion outcome and exact source/candidate/contract lineage
Changed logs, stale obligations, substituted manifests, missing objects, and invalid review or execution evidence refuse completion
Readable IDs, reference resolution, legacy access, and export/reload work through actual workflow entry points
criteria.when: It queries compact records and checks final completion with valid and deliberately altered evidence

criteria.given: Stable artifact items have actual dependency edges including spec-to-plan, plan-to-task, task-to-test, shared constraints, and other existing input relationships
then: Each edge pins a qualified numeric source item and exact numeric revision, resolving through the separate integrity file to its exact source snapshot, path, and stable item ID; Git preserves source history
Deterministic format-specific comparison covers meaningful item content and declared bindings; ownership and ordinary lookup links do not invent dependencies
Revalidation records exact old/new numeric revisions and resolved contexts, decision, and attribution under the artifact type existing review/coordinator authority requirements

A meaningful content or dependency-binding change publishes a fresh consumer item revision; unchanged content and bindings retain their revision and unrelated snapshot changes alone cause no revision churn
Pointer or checksum edits cannot establish derivation or transfer approval; original historical bindings are preserved
Execution records retain exact original test/source/runner/contract bindings; reuse obeys existing eligibility rules and otherwise requires new execution
criteria.when: The workflow records dependencies or revalidates an item against changed inputs

criteria.given: A graph has two independent item chains sharing document files, shared constraints, and multiple-input descendants
then: Direct consumers need reassessment; actual downstream descendants are potentially affected rather than automatically requiring new artifact revisions
Unrelated items remain eligible despite sharing a changed file; global constraints affect all actual linked consumers
Unresolved affected paths block new-context completion, and multiple-input consumers require every relevant path to be resolved
A reviewed retain decision can clear downstream potential impact only when consumer-relevant content, obligations, and dependency contract are unchanged and existing reuse rules permit it
A revise decision propagates reassessment to actual consumers of the changed item; unchanged payload alone is insufficient to clear impact
Historical bindings remain intact and cycles, ambiguous identities, and missing targets still fail explicitly
criteria.when: Only one upstream item changes meaningfully in the candidate Git snapshot

criteria.given: A deleted requirement or other artifact item has exclusive dependents and dependents serving additional active obligations
then: Deleted inputs cannot count as satisfied; their consumers need reassessment
Retired items leave the default active workflow while remaining retrievable with original bindings, evidence, and retirement decisions in Git history
Shared dependents remain active when justified through an explicit reviewed dependency update; downstream deletion or executable-test removal is not automatic
Stale active items and retired historical items have distinct states; resulting content/binding changes propagate through actual dependency edges
criteria.when: Deletion impact is assessed and reviewed outcomes are applied

criteria.given: Workstreams own committed artifact and dependency declarations, with a shared policy, qualified edges crossing workstream branches, independent chains, and duplicate local IDs under distinct owners
then: Discovery includes committed dependency declarations from all relevant workstream sources, not only files in the current checkout; cross-workstream references identify explicit owner, parent-qualified numeric item, and exact numeric revision, resolving its pinned snapshot/path/item through separate integrity data

Traversal follows actual edges across owners: a shared policy reaches every linked direct consumer and potentially affected descendant, while an isolated requirement change leaves independent chains eligible
Impact reports identify each affected owner, item, and dependency path without transferring write, reassessment, implementation, or acceptance authority between workstreams

Missing owner declarations, unavailable objects or dependency sources, stale indexes, and unsupported formats produce an explicit incomplete result and cannot silently clear affected paths or establish project-wide completeness

Cross-workstream cycles, conflicting identities, and deletion or retirement impact follow the same validation rules as local edges; derived indexes remain rebuildable and grant no acceptance authority
criteria.when: A referenced item changes and project-wide impact is computed from explicit source and candidate snapshots
